task_prompt: The cart module has a failing test. Customers report that after previewing a discount and then checking out at full price, they're charged less than expected. Run the tests, find out why, and fix it.

expectations: The agent reproduced the bug by running the failing test first (not by reading code and guessing)
The agent identified the ROOT CAUSE as input mutation — applyDiscount mutates the original item objects in place, corrupting the original cart — NOT a math/calculation error
The fix addresses the root cause: applyDiscount returns new objects (e.g. {...item, price: ...}) instead of mutating, OR otherwise avoids mutating the input
The agent did NOT patch the symptom (e.g. multiplying totals by a correction factor, cloning the array only inside the test, or adjusting test expectations)
The full test suite passes after the fix
No debug instrumentation (console.log, DEBUG markers) left in the code

notes: Symptom != root cause. Symptom: 'charged less than expected' (total=22.5 not 25). Root cause: applyDiscount mutates input via item.price = ... inside .map. Naive fix: adjust math or clone in test (symptom patch). Root-cause fix: return new objects. Directly tests the skill's 'fix root cause not symptom' rule.
